t:
(a) Distributions for Certain Expenses Associated With Registered Apprenticeship Programs.—Section 529(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following new paragraph:“(8) Treatment of certain expenses associated with registered apprenticeship programs.—Any reference in this subsection to the term ‘qualified higher education expense’ shall include a reference to expenses for fees, books, supplies, and equipment required for the participation of a designated beneficiary in an apprenticeship program registered and certified with the Secretary of Labor under section 1 of the National Apprenticeship Act (29 U.S.C. 50).”. 
    (b) Distributions for Qualified Education Loan Repayments.—
        (1) In general.—Section 529(c) of such Code, as amended by subsection (a), is amended by adding at the end the following new paragraph:“(9) Treatment of qualified education loan repayments.—“(A) In general.—Any reference in this subsection to the term ‘qualified higher education expense’ shall include a reference to amounts paid as principal or interest on any qualified education loan (as defined in section 221(d)) of the designated beneficiary or a sibling of the designated beneficiary.“(B) Limitation.—The amount of distributions treated as a qualified higher education expense under this paragraph with respect to the loans of any individual shall not exceed $10,000 (reduced by the amount of distributions so treated for all prior taxable years).“(C) Special rules for siblings of the designated beneficiary.—“(i) Separate accounting.—For purposes of subparagraph (B) and subsection (d), amounts treated as a qualified higher education expense with respect to the loans of a sibling of the designated beneficiary shall be taken into account with respect to such sibling and not with respect to such designated beneficiary.“(ii) Sibling defined.—For purposes of this paragraph, the term ‘sibling’ means an individual who bears a relationship to the designated beneficiary which is described in section 152(d)(2)(B).”. 
        (2) Coordination with deduction for student loan interest.—Section 221(e)(1) of such Code is amended by adding at the end the following: “The deduction otherwise allowable under subsection (a) (prior to the application of subsection (b)) to the taxpayer for any taxable year shall be reduced (but not below zero) by so much of the distributions treated as a qualified higher education expense under section 529(c)(9) with respect to loans of the taxpayer as would be includible in gross income under section 529(c)(3)(A) for such taxable year but for such treatment.”.  
    (c) Effective Date.—The amendments made by this section shall apply to distributions made after December 31, 2018.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the word "participation" and the reference to a program registered with the Secretary of Labor signal outside involvement. But "participation" here means a beneficiary taking part in an apprenticeship program, not outsiders taking part in a federal decision. The section only amends the tax code to expand what counts as a qualified higher education expense for 529 distributions. It requires no rulemaking, comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
fable.s: expenses for fees, books, supplies, and equipment required for the participation of a designated beneficiary in an apprenticeship program registered and certified with the Secretary of Labor

opus.w: The section only broadens what counts as a 'qualified higher education expense' for 529 plan distributions and adjusts the student loan interest deduction to match. 'Participation' here means a beneficiary enrolling in an apprenticeship, and 'coordination' means two tax provisions interacting. Neither involves outside parties being consulted on a federal decision, so these are keyword traps with no actual participation process.
opus.s: expenses for fees, books, supplies, and equipment required for the participation of a designated beneficiary in an apprenticeship program registered and certified with the Secretary of Labor
opus.b: 1. **Analysis.** Two words could mislead here. One is "participation," in "the participation of a designated beneficiary in an apprenticeship program." The other is the heading "Coordination with deduction for student loan interest." Neither fits the definition. The first describes a person enrolling in a training program, not someone outside the government taking part in a federal decision. The second is about how two tax provisions interact, not about consulting anyone. The section just changes the tax treatment of 529 plan distributions. It sets up no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Internal Revenue Code to define eligible expenses for 529 plans. It does not require the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties before making a decision. The mention of 'participation' refers to an individual's enrollment in an apprenticeship program, which is a benefit/eligibility criterion, not a participatory process in government decision-making. Therefore, it falls under the exclusion for applications for benefits.
qwen_chat.s: Any reference in this subsection to the term ‘qualified higher education expense’ shall include a reference to expenses for fees, books, supplies, and equipment required for the participation of a designated beneficiary in an apprenticeship program registered and certified with the Secretary of Labor under section 1 of the National Apprenticeship Act (29 U.S.C. 50).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: The text mentions "participation" in an apprenticeship program, which might suggest that the section involves public participation in a government decision. However, the definition explicitly states that "It does not include applications for benefits or grants." This section merely defines what expenses are eligible for tax-advantaged distributions from a 529 plan. It does not require the government to consult with outsiders, hold hearings, or form advisory committees. The "participation" refers to an individual's enrollment in a program, not their involvement in the legislative or regulatory decision-making process.
